# Setup checklist

<!-- Generated by `pnpm hub docs` from app/apps/installer/src/steps. Do not edit; change the step instead. -->

Work top to bottom. `hub doctor` runs every box below that is not an optional extra and prints PASS, WARN or FAIL per step id; `hub doctor --automation` adds the extras. A FAIL names its own fix. `hub guide` prints the by-hand steps. Which access goes to what: `@docs/setup/access.md`.

## Tools

- [ ] **Node.js 22.20 or newer** (`tools.node`)
  - Proves: `node --version` reports 22.20 or newer.
  - You: Install Node 22.20 or newer, for example with nvm: `nvm install 22`. Open a new terminal and run `node --version`.
- [ ] **pnpm** (`tools.pnpm`)
  - Proves: `pnpm --version` answers.
  - You: Run `corepack enable pnpm` (ships with Node) or `npm i -g pnpm`.
- [ ] **Claude Code CLI** (`tools.claude`)
  - Proves: `claude --version` answers.
  - You: Install Claude Code from https://claude.com/claude-code and sign in once interactively with `claude`.
## Files

- [ ] **Working folders** (`files.dirs`)
  - Proves: `state/runs`, `state/clients`, `state/history` and `state/secrets` (the git-ignored secrets folder, not readable by others) exist.
  - `hub install` fixes it: Creates the folders; the secrets folder gets mode 700.
- [ ] **Config files (never overwritten)** (`files.config`)
  - Proves: `config/mcp.json` exists and parses.
  - `hub install` fixes it: Copies a default from `app/apps/installer/templates/` only when the file is missing.
- [ ] **Settings file (never overwritten)** (`files.settings`; optional extra, `--automation`)
  - Proves: `config.json` exists, parses and has every required key.
  - `hub install` fixes it: Copies a default from `app/apps/installer/templates/` only when the file is missing.
- [ ] **Project .mcp.json** (`files.mcp-json`)
  - Proves: `.mcp.json` contains every server of `config/mcp.json` (stdio programs as absolute paths under the core), and every stdio server command in it exists.
  - `hub install` fixes it: Merges the servers of `config/mcp.json` into `.mcp.json` with stdio paths made absolute under the core, keeps your other servers, saves a one-time `.mcp.json.bak`.
- [ ] **App database** (`files.app-db`)
  - Proves: The database file exists (`data/app.db` of the instance).
  - `hub install` fixes it: Runs the app's `db:migrate` script (`pnpm --dir app run db:migrate`).
## Skills

- [ ] **UI skills for development (coss, coss-particles)** (`skills.dev`; UI development only)
  - Proves: `~/.claude/skills/coss` and `coss-particles` exist.
  - `hub install` fixes it: `npx skills add https://github.com/cosscom/ui.git --skill coss --skill coss-particles -a claude-code -g -y`.
- [ ] **Agent skills linked into Claude** (`skills.runtime`)
  - Proves: Every `skills/<name>/` is a symlink in `~/.claude/skills/` pointing at this folder.
  - `hub install` fixes it: `ln -sfn` per skill; a real folder of the same name is never replaced.
## Projects

- [ ] **Projects (one folder each)** (`projects.registry`)
  - Proves: Every `<projects>/<slug>/` has a non-empty `project.md` and a `knowledge/` folder. With no project yet there is nothing to check.
  - `hub install` fixes it: Creates the missing `knowledge/` folders. `project.md` is written by the project-setup skill, never by the installer.
## Instance

- [ ] **Instance matches the core** (`instance.core`)
  - Proves: `core.version` exists and names the core in use (core clean at that commit), the instance holds no core files, the core tracks no instance files, and generated skill links point at existing core skills.
## Admin

- [ ] **The admin listens on this machine only** (`admin.loopback`)
  - Proves: If the admin is running, the instance admin port (admin_port in config/config.json, or HUB_ADMIN_PORT; default 5173) answers on 127.0.0.1 and no listener is bound to every interface. Not running is fine.
  - You: Stop whatever listens on the admin port, then start the admin with `hub up`; it always binds 127.0.0.1.
## Server

- [ ] **The local server answers** (`server.health`)
  - Proves: If something listens on the instance API port (api_port in config/config.json, or HUB_PORT; default 4317), it listens on 127.0.0.1 only and `GET /api/health` answers 200 with `ok`. Not running is a WARN (`hub up` starts it), never a pass: this step says nothing about a server that is not there.
  - You: Start it with `hub up` (it binds 127.0.0.1). If the port is held by something else, change `api_port` in `config/config.json`.
## MCP

- [ ] **knowledge-mcp starts** (`mcp.knowledge`)
  - Proves: The `knowledge-mcp` command of `.mcp.json` is started exactly as Claude would start it and answers an MCP `initialize`. It runs against a throw-away empty database, so the real `data/app.db` is never opened; the process is closed at once.
  - You: Run `hub install --only files.mcp-json` (writes the server with absolute paths), then `pnpm install` in the core's `app/` if the program is missing.
## Mail

- [ ] **mail-mcp daemon** (`mail.daemon`)
  - Proves: `localhost:8787` answers an MCP `initialize` (however mail-mcp was started).
  - You: Install: `brew install dastrobu/tap/mail-mcp`. Start it as a service: `brew services start mail-mcp`.
- [ ] **Mail account and permissions** (`mail.account`; optional extra, `--automation`)
  - Proves: mail-mcp lists the account named in `config/config.json` and reads one message from its first mailbox.
  - You: Open Mail.app and add the account (System Settings > Internet Accounts). Keep Mail.app running. Put the account's exact name in `config/config.json` (`account`) and the allowed sender addresses in `allow_list`. When macOS asks, allow `mail-mcp` to control Mail (Privacy & Security > Automation) and allow Accessibility (needed to create drafts). Full Disk Access is only needed if a tool reads `~/Library/Mail` directly; the default setup does not.
## Messengers

- [ ] **Telegram bot token for the receive-only poller (optional)** (`messengers.token`; optional extra, `--automation`)
  - Proves: `state/secrets/telegram-bot-token` holds one `<digits>:<secret>` line and is mode 600. The value is never printed.
  - You: Open @BotFather in Telegram, send /newbot and make a bot just for this app. Store the token alone in `state/secrets/telegram-bot-token` (`pnpm hub token telegram` if available, otherwise paste into the file) and run `chmod 600` on it.
- [ ] **Telegram accepts the bot token** (`telegram.getme`; optional extra, `--automation`)
  - Proves: Telegram's `getMe` answers for the token in `state/secrets/telegram-bot-token` (one read-only call; the bot's @name is shown, the token never). WARN when there is no token file (the feature is off) or Telegram cannot be reached; FAIL when Telegram refuses the token or the shape is wrong.
  - You: If Telegram refuses the token: in @BotFather send /token (or /revoke) for the bot, then store the new one with `pnpm hub token telegram`.
- [ ] **The messengers poller is running inside the server** (`messengers.poller`; optional extra, `--automation`)
  - Proves: `GET /api/health` on the local server reports `messengers.state` = `running` with a poll in the last 5 minutes. WARN when the server is down or the feature is off without a token.
## Notion

- [ ] **Notion integration token** (`notion.token`; optional extra, `--automation`)
  - Proves: The token file is stored with mode 600 and Notion accepts it (`GET /users/me`). Which databases it reaches is the next step, `notion.access`.
  - You: Easiest: `pnpm hub setup` asks for the token and checks it with `GET /users/me`. By hand: Open https://www.notion.so/profile/integrations and create an internal integration; copy its secret. In Notion, open the CRM teamspace (or each CRM database), choose Connections and add the integration. Store the token: `pnpm hub token notion` (hidden prompt; writes `state/secrets/notion-token`, mode 600). Which databases it must reach, and what to share, is checked by `notion.access`.
- [ ] **The integration reaches every database of every project** (`notion.access`; optional extra, `--automation`)
  - Proves: For every project that lists Notion databases: each database in project.md answers to the integration (shared, readable, capability Read content), is not archived and not in the trash, and every database its relations point at (Leads, People, ...) is reachable and live too. A failure names the database and says to share it with the integration under Connections. Read only: GET requests. WARN when there is no token to test with.
  - You: In Notion open the project's teamspace root page, choose `...` > Connections and add the integration. Sub-pages and databases inherit it; a database that was moved out loses it, so share again after a move. The integration needs the capability Read content (Notion > Settings > Integrations > your integration > Capabilities). It never writes. An archived database is not a grant problem: point project.md at the live database (`## Notion databases`) or restore it in Notion.
- [ ] **Notion connector in the session** (`notion.connector`)
  - Proves: `.mcp.json` lists the `notion` server (hint only: whether you have signed in to it is seen inside a session, with `/mcp`).
  - You: In Claude Code run `/mcp` once and sign in to `notion`; in Claude Desktop enable the Notion connector in Settings > Connectors.
## Backup

- [ ] **Code and instance are pushed off this machine** (`backup.git`; `hub doctor` only; setup and install never run it)
  - Proves: For the instance and the core (and any path listed in `backup_repos` of `config/config.json`): an `origin` remote exists and the local HEAD commit is on it (`git ls-remote origin`: the tip, or an ancestor of a tip already fetched). FAIL: no origin, or HEAD not pushed. WARN: origin cannot be reached. Nothing is pushed.
  - You: No remote: create a PRIVATE repository, `git remote add origin <url>`, then push. HEAD not on origin: `git push` (for the core, push the commit the instance pins). Other repositories to watch (for example the plan repository): list their paths in `backup_repos` in `config/config.json`.
- [ ] **The app database can be copied and the copy is sound** (`backup.db`; `hub doctor` only; setup and install never run it)
  - Proves: `data/app.db` is opened READ-ONLY, `VACUUM INTO` writes a copy into a temporary folder, the copy passes `PRAGMA integrity_check` and its rows are counted; the temporary folder is then removed. The live file is never written. It proves a good copy is possible, not that one is kept: copy `data/app.db` somewhere off the machine yourself.
  - You: Integrity failure: stop the server (`hub up` window), keep `data/app.db` and `data/app.db-wal` untouched and restore the last good copy. Keep a regular off-machine copy: `sqlite3 data/app.db "VACUUM INTO '<folder>/app-<date>.db'"` (safe while the server runs).
- [ ] **The Notion dump is recent and restorable** (`backup.notion`; `hub doctor` only; setup and install never run it)
  - Proves: For every project that lists Notion databases: the newest dump (a folder with `manifest.json`) is at most 7 days old and recorded no database error, and `notion-dump restore <project> --dry-run` passes (it reads the dump and the live databases and says what a restore would do; it never writes to Notion, and a restore itself is never run). WARN when there is no token to read the live databases with.
  - You: Dump: `pnpm --filter @hub/notion notion-dump dump <project folder>` (needs the integration token and `notion.access` green). Dry run by hand: `pnpm --filter @hub/notion notion-dump restore <project folder> --dry-run`.
- [ ] **Secret files exist with the right modes** (`backup.secrets`; `hub doctor` only; setup and install never run it)
  - Proves: The secrets folder is mode 700, every secret file in it is mode 600, and each token file a project names (`notion.token_file`) exists. Only names and modes are read; no value is opened. Keeping an off-machine copy of the folder is yours to do and to remember: nothing here can see it.
  - You: `chmod 700 state/secrets` and `chmod 600 state/secrets/*`. Keep one off-machine copy of `state/secrets/` (a password manager or an encrypted drive).

Update this page when the architecture changes.
